screenplay.text:
STORMWATER

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     EXT. SUBURBAN STREET - DAY                              1

               Heavy rain. Gutters run like rivers. A storm drain at the
               kerb gulps brown water.

               A small scruffy terrier, BISCUIT, splashes after a tennis
               ball. The ball bounces once, twice, and drops through the
               grate of the STORM DRAIN.

               Biscuit squeezes through the gap after it and vanishes.

               REFILWE (11), yellow raincoat, red gumboots, runs down the
               pavement holding an empty lead.

                                     REFILWE
                         Biscuit! Biscuit, no!

               She drops to her knees at the drain. From below, faint and
               echoing, a bark.

         2     INT. MUNICIPAL DEPOT - OFFICE - DAY                     2

               A prefab office. Hard hats on hooks. A kettle and a map of
               the town's drains pinned to the wall.

               MR. VAN DER MERWE (50s), orange overalls, big moustache,
               eats a sandwich at his desk. A phone rings. He answers with
               his mouth full.

                                     MR. VAN DER MERWE
                         Depot.

                                     REFILWE (V.O.)
                               (on the phone, crying)
                         My dog is in the drain on Acacia
                         Street and he can't get out!

               He puts down the sandwich.

         3     EXT. SUBURBAN STREET - DAY                              3

               A municipal truck with an orange light pulls up. Mr. Van der
               Merwe climbs down with a crowbar and a torch. His young
               colleague, SIBUSISO (20s), follows with a coil of rope.

               Refilwe points at the drain.

                                     REFILWE
                         He went in there.

               Mr. Van der Merwe levers up the heavy steel MANHOLE COVER
               beside the drain. It clanks onto the road.








                                                                       2.


               He shines his torch down a ladder into the dark. Water roars
               somewhere below.

                                     SIBUSISO
                         The pipe runs under three streets.
                         He could be anywhere.

                                     REFILWE
                         He follows the ball. He always
                         follows the ball.

         4     INT. STORMWATER TUNNEL - CONTINUOUS                     4

               A round concrete tunnel, knee-deep in rushing water. Torch
               beams bounce off the curved walls.

               Mr. Van der Merwe and Sibusiso wade forward. Sibusiso's rope
               is tied around his waist.

                                     SIBUSISO
                         Biscuit! Here, boy!

               Only the water answers.

                                     MR. VAN DER MERWE
                               (stopping)
                         Shh. Listen.

               A bark. Ahead and to the left.

         5     INT. STORMWATER TUNNEL - JUNCTION - CONTINUOUS          5

               Two tunnels meet. On a narrow concrete ledge above the
               water, Biscuit stands shivering, the tennis ball in his
               mouth.

               Mr. Van der Merwe reaches up. Biscuit backs away, growling
               around the ball.

                                     MR. VAN DER MERWE
                         He won't come.

                                     SIBUSISO
                         He won't leave the ball.

               Sibusiso thinks. Then he pulls a second tennis ball from his
               overall pocket, a bit chewed.

                                     MR. VAN DER MERWE
                         Why do you have a tennis ball?

                                     SIBUSISO
                         Why don't you?









                                                                       3.


               He holds it up and squeaks it. Biscuit drops the first ball
               and leaps straight into Sibusiso's arms.

         6     EXT. SUBURBAN STREET - DAY                              6

               The rain has stopped. Neighbours stand under umbrellas
               around the open manhole.

               Sibusiso climbs out of the hole with Biscuit inside his
               overalls, only the dog's head poking out. The neighbours
               clap.

               Refilwe runs to them. Biscuit licks her face all over.

                                     REFILWE
                         Thank you! Thank you!

               Mr. Van der Merwe climbs out last, soaked to the chest. He
               holds up the first tennis ball, dripping.

                                     MR. VAN DER MERWE
                         He'll want this too.

                                     REFILWE
                               (laughing)
                         Keep it. You earned it.

               He looks at the ball. He puts it in his pocket.

                                                            FADE OUT.

shots.source:
Heavy rain. Gutters run like rivers. A storm drain at the kerb gulps brown water.
A small scruffy terrier, BISCUIT, splashes after a tennis ball. The ball bounces once, twice, and drops through the grate of the STORM DRAIN.
shots.rationale: Establishes the storm drain and the ball's fall in a single, immersive view.

shots.source:
Biscuit squeezes through the gap after it and vanishes.
REFILWE (11), yellow raincoat, red gumboots, runs down the pavement holding an empty lead.
shots.rationale: Frames Refilwe's distressed reaction as she kneels to call the dog.

shots.source:
Biscuit! Biscuit, no!
She drops to her knees at the drain. From below, faint and echoing, a bark.
shots.rationale: Tightens on Refilwe's face as she listens to the echoing bark from below.

MR. VAN DER MERWE (50s), orange overalls, big moustache, eats a sandwich at his desk. A phone rings. He answers with his mouth full.
shots.rationale: Establishes the office space and Mr. Van Der Merwe's relaxed eating before the phone interruption.

shots.source:
Depot.
My dog is in the drain on Acacia Street and he can't get out!
shots.rationale: Captures Mr. Van Der Merwe's reaction to the distressing news about the dog in the drain.

shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue about the pipe's path and the dog's behavior.

shots.rationale: Establishes the oppressive tunnel space and the men's precarious position before dialogue begins.

shots.source:

shots.rationale: Focuses on Sibusiso's call, emphasizing his isolation and the emptiness of the tunnel.

shots.source: Shh. Listen.
shots.rationale: Captures Mr. Van der Merwe's sudden silence, preparing the audience for the shift in tone.

shots.source: A bark. Ahead and to the left.
shots.rationale: Pan reveals the source of the bark, guiding the eye through the curved tunnel space.

shots.source:
Two tunnels meet. On a narrow concrete ledge above the water, Biscuit stands shivering, the tennis ball in his mouth.
Mr. Van der Merwe reaches up. Biscuit backs away, growling around the ball.
shots.rationale: Establishes the physical tension and the ball's central role in the standoff.

shots.source:

He won't leave the ball.
shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue exchange about Biscuit's reluctance without distraction.

shots.source:

Why don't you?
shots.rationale: Frames the reveal of the second ball and the playful challenge between the men.

shots.source: He holds it up and squeaks it. Biscuit drops the first ball and leaps straight into Sibusiso's arms.
shots.rationale: Emphasizes the emotional payoff as Biscuit leaps into Sibusiso's arms.

Sibusiso climbs out of the hole with Biscuit inside his overalls, only the dog's head poking out. The neighbours clap.

shots.rationale: Refilwe's gratitude and the dog's affection are best captured intimately.

shots.rationale: The exchange of the ball between Mr. Van der Merwe and Refilwe needs a clear medium view.

shots.rationale: Mr. Van der Merwe's reluctant acceptance of the ball is a tight focus on his action.
